text:
sre-oncall: FYI opening incident thread - we're seeing elevated P95/P99 latency and increased 5xx for Dedicated inference pools in us-east-1 starting ~10:12 EDT. Symptoms look like long warmup + occasional host-level GPU thermal backoffs. Creating timeline here. /cc @channel

ops-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-gpu-pool p99-latency > 1.8s (us-east-1)

miguel: Noted. I'm seeing a pattern of pods reporting long model load times then repeated kernel resets on a subset of nodes (gpu-node-ax*). Collecting node logs and dmesg.

anya: Customer impact: Dedicated tenants on us-east-1 with large-replicas models saw inference errors and slow starts; some busy request bursts got 502s as worker processes crashed and restarted. Support queue has 6 active tickets.

infra: I throttled new placement to avoid scheduling onto the suspect host pool and forced a graceful drain of gpu-node-ax[03..06]. Also applied a temporary per-node model-concurrency cap to reduce sustained power draw.

ops-bot: [ACTION] drain started at 10:18 EDT; 4 nodes cordoned. Autoscaler stopped placing new jobs on pool-us-east-g2.

miguel: Log excerpt from affected pod:
```
2026-05-11T10:13:26Z WARN modelloader: load_time=12.4s model=llm-xlarge
2026-05-11T10:13:31Z ERROR kernel: GPU thermal event: throttle=THROTTLE_REASON_TEMP, temp=92C
2026-05-11T10:13:35Z ERROR runtime: process crashed with code 137 (OOM/KILL) on device 0
```

anya: Mitigations in place: 1) drain and reprovision suspect hosts, 2) capped per-GPU concurrency to 2 inference workers, 3) routed overflow Dedicated requests to us-east-2 and us-west-1 cluster pools while we stabilize.

infra: Commands used (short):
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-ax03 -n infra-us-east
kubectl drain gpu-node-ax03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n infra-us-east
fluxctl set image deploy/dedicated-pool concurrency-cap=2
```

ops-bot: [METRICS] Initial effect: 5xx rate for dedicated pools in us-east-1 down from 3.6% -> 0.9% within 8m after routing and caps. P99 latency improving but tail still elevated as warmups finish.

miguel: Root cause hypothesis: a recent kernel/driver combo plus a change in our model hotplug candidate list led to sustained peak GPU power draw during concurrent model loads causing thermal throttling and rare watchdog kills. Repro on staging with stress load.

anya: Customer comms: Drafted short status page entry and templated support reply offering priority assistance and optional migration to other regions. Will publish at 10:30 EDT unless ops objects. Preview: https://status.redwood.infra/incidents/1755000000-preview

infra: Next actions: 1) repro locally and capture driver traces, 2) roll nodes to a driver build with conservative power management, 3) implement preflight that simulates N concurrent model loads during scale-up, 4) add a cluster-level soft-cap to avoid hitting thermal thresholds.

support: I'll send the standard notice to affected Dedicated customers and flag any high-priority tenants for manual migration assistance.

status-bot: [STATUS PAGE] Draft ready. Will publish at 10:30 EDT: https://status.redwood.infra/incidents/1755000000

sre-oncall: ETA to normal: 20-45 minutes for node drains, reprovision, and backlog drain. We'll close this thread once 5xx <0.5% and p99 latency back to baseline for 15m.

miguel: Assigning postmortem owner: @miguel. I'll collect timeline, node traces, driver diffs, and remediation actions. Target incident report: EOD today.

ops-bot: [RUNBOOK] https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-thermal-throttle.md | Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-gpu/us-east-1?orgId=1

sre-oncall: Thanks team. Keep updates short; escalate to pager if we see regression.

infra: Update 10:42 EDT - drains complete for cordoned nodes, replacement nodes coming up with updated driver, routing persists. 5xx now ~0.6%.

support: Sent notices to customers at 10:44 EDT. 2 customers requested assisted migration; facilitating now.

miguel: Update 10:50 EDT - driver build rolled to 2/4 replacement nodes, warmup looks stable there. Continuing rollout and monitoring.

ops-bot: [MONITOR] 5xx=0.4% p99 trending down. If stable for 15m we'll move to resolved state.
